item.title: Kagoshima Ramen — Guide
item.description: Kagoshima ramen holds a special place as one of the oldest tonkotsu (pork-bone) ramen styles in Kyushu, having developed somewhat independently of the famous Hakata ramen of Fukuoka. Its broth is a rich but comparatively mild and mellow tonkotsu, often blended with chicken bones and vegetables and typically semi-cloudy rather than intensely thick, giving a rounder, gentler flavour. It’s served with medium-thick, straight noodles (unlike Hakata’s thin noodles), topped with chāshū pork, spring onion, beansprouts and sometimes cabbage.
